summary: Console sessionization causing single streaming API call to be recorded as multiple usage sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer VeloxAI reports that single streaming generate calls are being split into multiple 'sessions' in the Console usage analytics, resulting in inflated session counts and mismatched per-session metrics in dashboards and billing exports. Impact: Overcounted sessions and per-session latency/length metrics; potential billing discrepancies for a major customer on Dedicated tier. Observed since 2026-03-08 after a streaming proxy rollout.

Context: VeloxAI uses long-lived streaming sessions for multi-turn generation. Console aggregates usage by a session_id field derived during request ingest. When their streaming client briefly reconnects (common under mobile networks), our pipeline currently creates a new session_id instead of continuing the existing logical session, creating multiple session records for one logical interaction.
impact: Customer-visible: dashboards show 2–6x more sessions for streaming routes vs raw logs. Billing export shows session-count deltas for VeloxAI (estimated +18% sessions last 7 days). Business: Dedicated customer concerned about overbilling and product analytics integrity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer starts a streaming generate request with a persistent client-side session token (client-session: abc123).
2) Simulate intermittent network blips causing the client to reconnect the stream (close and re-open WebSocket within 10s).
3) Observe Console > Usage > Sessions for the route: two distinct session entries appear with separate session_id values even though the client-session token is identical.
4) Export usage CSV for the timeframe and compare session_count vs raw request logs (requestid-level): raw logs show 1 logical session, Console shows multiple.

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer reported spikes in session_count for streaming routes; attached CSVs and raw requestids. Asking for triage and measurement of billing exposure.

2026-03-11 - Tom Reynolds (SRE): Reproduced locally with simulated transient disconnects. Observed new session_id emitted on reconnect. Captured example logs and trace ids. Marked as P1 due to billing impact. Kicked to infra team.

2026-03-12 - Lina Chen (Platform Eng): Hypothesis: sessionization relies on 'websocket_conn_id' as identity when present; reconnect gets new conn id and ingest creates new session record. Proposed fix: fallback to client_session header if present and continue session when delta < 30s.

2026-03-13 - VeloxAI (Customer): Confirmed they include a client-session header in their SDK; reported that reconnects are frequent for mobile users. Customer requests urgent workaround and rollback option for the streaming proxy rollout.

2026-03-14 - Tom Reynolds (SRE): Implemented temporary ingestion rule to prefer client_session header when available. Patch deployed to prod us-east and VeloxAI reports preliminary alignment between sessions and raw logs. Preparing PR for permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Ingest pipeline stages: streaming-proxy -> kafka topic 'ingest-raw' -> sessionizer service -> analytics rollup. Sessionizer currently keys on websocket_conn_id when present, else request_token. Issue triggered when client sends persistent client_session header but websocket_conn_id changes on reconnect.

Correlation of request_ids shows that reconnect events keep client_session but generate a new websocket_conn_id. Sessionizer creates new session node because websocket_conn_id was considered authoritative.
Billing export job aggregates by session_id produced by sessionizer. Fix must preserve logical session continuity to avoid billing noise.

Tested quick patch in staging that checks for client_session header and if seen, attempts to reconcile with last session for that client_session within a 60s window. Staging results show sessions no longer split for reconnect scenarios.

Risk: naive reconciliation could join unrelated concurrent sessions if client_session is reused across different tabs or users. Need a safer tie-breaker (e.g., compare last activity timestamp + IP fingerprint + request sequence number).
Related past tickets: SUP-42188 (console usage unique-client-spike missing requestid) indicated edge cases in session attribution; learned patterns reused here.
Observed affected_models were the routes most used by VeloxAI (gptx-mini for chat, gptx-embedder-v2 for embeddings), but root cause is transport/sessionization logic and not model-specific.
resolution: Workaround (prod hotfix): Temporarily prefer 'client_session' header for session continuation when websocket_conn_id changes and last_activity < 60s. Hotfix deployed to us-east on 2026-03-14 (rollout id: rollout-20260314-psi).

Permanent fix: Platform Eng to land PR that enhances sessionizer to use a safe reconciliation heuristic (client_session + last_activity + IP_fingerprint) and adds an opt-in console toggle to control session merge behavior. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2894 (in review).

Customer communication: Sent VeloxAI a status note and temporary credits offer while we validate corrected billing exports. Customer accepted: credits capped at $5k for the affected billing period pending final audit.

Follow-ups: Add an automated analytics test for reconnect scenarios in the ingress e2e suite; update confluence runbook and alert thresholds to detect sudden session_count drift (>15% over 24h). Assigned to Lina Chen for rollout plan and Tom Reynolds for monitoring updates.
